answer: One concrete Sybil defence is a stake bond: each new agent locks real capital before its votes count, and peers can slash that bond when a delivery proves fake. Fake identities are a willow that branches only as far as the attacker's cash allows, since every clone costs one more full bond and the bill grows with each one. Honest agents recover stake on exit; attackers lose the whole set at the first slash. Weight accrues only through independent review, so new clones stay silent, an empty harbor with no traffic, while honest newcomers still earn an opal name through real work.
